items.title: CBSA Dog Aggie Flags 16 Kilograms of Undeclared Goat Feet and Ghee at Pearson
items.summary: According to the Canada Border Services Agency, detector dog Aggie intercepted another large shipment of undeclared food at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. The agency reports the seizure included 16 kilograms of goat feet, chicken, ghee and milk powder brought in by a group of travellers arriving from Pakistan. CBSA says the travellers were fined $1,350 for failing to declare the items. The agency reports this is the latest in a series of food and animal product seizures publicized at Pearson throughout 2026. According to the CBSA, Canadian law requires travellers to declare all food, plant and animal products entering the country. The agency says undeclared or improperly permitted goods can be confiscated, destroyed or ordered removed from Canada.

items.title: Morguard Marks Topping-Off of 431-Unit Rental Project Near Cawthra and Atwater
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Morguard Corporation held a topping-off ceremony this month for its Boulevard on the Green rental development at 725 Village Green Blvd. in Mississauga, with occupancy expected to begin next year. The outlet reports Brian Athey, Morguard's senior vice president of development, said the fully enclosed building marked the milestone with a ceremonial glass plaque guests were invited to sign. Insauga.com says the project, which broke ground in October 2024 near Cawthra Road and Atwater Avenue, will bring 431 new purpose-built rental units to the city across three mid-rise buildings and townhomes. According to the outlet, the property's zoning allowed for towers up to 12 storeys, but Athey said Morguard chose a lower-rise design to fit the surrounding neighbourhood of single-family homes and townhomes. The outlet reports Morguard has owned the roughly 20-year-vacant site, previously believed to have housed a postal sorting facility, for about two decades.

items.title: Dense Fog Prompts Near-Zero Visibility Warning Across Mississauga and Nine Other Municipalities
items.summary: According to Environment and Climate Change Canada, a yellow-level weather advisory is in effect Thursday morning for Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon, Halton Hills, Burlington, Oakville, Newmarket, Georgina and northern York Region. The agency says areas of dense fog are expected to impact the region, with visibility suddenly dropping to near zero at times. Environment Canada reports travel will likely be hazardous in some locations as a result. The agency is advising drivers to prepare for near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach their destinations. According to Environment Canada, the fog is expected to dissipate later in the morning.

items.title: Mississauga Animal Services Cuts Adoption Fees to $25 for Two-Week Adopt-a-thon
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Mississauga Animal Services is reducing adoption fees to $25, plus HST and any applicable licence fees, for all dogs and cats during an Adopt-a-thon running Nov. 2 to 14. The city says the discount is a significant markdown from regular fees, which typically run $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens. According to the city, the event aims to find more shelter animals homes before winter, when adoptions typically slow down. The city reports the adoption event is open to everyone, with no appointment needed, though wait times may vary. According to the city, adopters must be at least 18 years old, and the shelter is located at 735 Central Parkway West.

items.title: City Clerk's Certification Puts Final Count at 191,166 Ballots Cast
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the city clerk has certified the results of the 2026 municipal election, confirming the mayor, 11 ward and regional councillors, and school board trustees for the 2026-2030 term. The city reports certification follows the Municipal Elections Act's requirement that all votes be counted and verified before results become official. According to the city, a total of 191,166 ballots were cast in the election. The city says the new council will take its oaths of office at an inaugural ceremony on Nov. 16 in the Main Auditorium at the Living Arts Centre, 4141 Living Arts Dr. According to the city, residents can view the complete certified results, including school board trustee results, on the city's elections webpage or by calling 905-615-VOTE.

items.title: Elliot Lake Drug Raid Nets Mississauga Man Among Two People Charged
items.summary: According to the Ontario Provincial Police, a Mississauga man is one of two people charged after officers executed a search warrant Tuesday night at an apartment in Elliot Lake, roughly 160 kilometres west of Sudbury. The OPP reports officers recovered a large quantity of hard drugs during the raid. According to police, the investigation involved the OPP's Community Street Crime Unit, Organized Crime Enforcement Bureau and the East Algoma detachment. The OPP identified the two people charged as 45-year-old Jennifer Stubbert of Elliot Lake and 20-year-old Kory Joseph-Labban of Mississauga. Police say both face numerous charges stemming from the drug seizure. According to the OPP, both were held in custody and scheduled to appear Wednesday in bail court at the Ontario Court of Justice in Blind River.
